explanation: The main character in the book of Joshua, a leader of the people of Israel after Moses' death, who led them into the promised land of Canaan.
The area that God had promised to give to the people of Israel, and which Joshua led them into to conquer and settle there.
A title used to describe Joshua, showing his obedience and devotion to God and His will.
To take control of a territory or nation by using military force, as Joshua and the Israelites did with Canaan.
The geographical areas that were divided among the twelve tribes of Israel, so that each tribe received its own land.
The twelve groups of the people of Israel who were descendants of Jacob's twelve sons. Each tribe was assigned a territory in Canaan.
The agreements between Joshua and the Israelites and the various Canaanite kings and cities they fought against and made treaties with.
A holy chest that contained the stone tablets with the Ten Commandments, and which symbolized God's presence among the people of Israel.
